requirements.requirement: Container runs as unprivileged appsvc user
requirements.summary: appsvc created as a normal unprivileged user (uid 1000, no sudo group); podman info run as appsvc confirms Rootless=true; webapp.service process tree (conmon/nginx) runs under appsvc's user manager (user@1000.service), not root.

curl to $NODE_IP:8080 returns HTTP 200 both before and after reboot; ss/listening-sockets snapshot confirms a pasta (rootless podman networking) listener on *:8080 owned by the appsvc container stack, matching the quadlet's PublishPort=8080:80.

requirements.requirement: Application starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
requirements.summary: Lingering enabled for appsvc (Linger=yes) so user@1000.service runs independent of login; webapp.service was generated from a podman quadlet and symlinked into default.target.wants (auto-start). loginctl list-sessions before and after showed only a manager-class session (no tty/seat), i.e. no interactive login. Crucially, a full node reboot was performed (boot_id changed from a70d7f83... to f4e419b2...), and post-reboot evidence directly shows Linger=yes persisted, no login session present, webapp.service active, and HTTP 200 on port 8080 — a genuine bounded-disruption-and-recovery demonstration rather than static configuration alone.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct, first-hand evidence: nginx runs rootless as appsvc on port 8080, and a genuine node reboot (boot_id changed) confirmed the service auto-starts via linger + quadlet + default.target.wants with no active login session, both before and after the disruption. Hygiene is good with only trivial leftover temp files and one harmless failed diagnostic command.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was captured; long-term persistence across multiple reboots or power-cycle edge cases is not directly evidenced.
Minor /tmp residue (dnf.pid, dnf_install.log) from package installation was not cleaned up, though this is low-risk and unrelated to the appsvc/container setup itself.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were tightly scoped to the task: package install, user creation, linger enablement, image pull, quadlet authoring, and service start/verify all map directly to the required outcome. One attempted `systemctl --user enable webapp.service` (cmd-210c585ad6be4ef1) failed harmlessly because quadlet-generated units cannot be enabled that way — a diagnostic misstep with no state change, not a real mutation. The dnf install log/pid files (/tmp/dnf.pid, /tmp/dnf_install.log) were left in /tmp per the after_executor snapshot rather than cleaned up, a minor low-risk residue. No failed services, no package-health issues, and no unnecessary or destructive mutations were found; the reboot itself was a necessary, task-relevant action to validate the boot-start requirement.
